sections.body: Fresh two-sigma departures and first evolving-VWAP touches are shown separately for ES, NQ and GC, with mirrored sides and four overlapping anchor populations. Ten two-minute candles means 20 minutes; fifty means 100 minutes. These values come from the full saved summary, whose longer-horizon rows were omitted from the earlier concise findings CSV.
sections.title: Question and selected scope

sections.body: Return probability depends strongly on the anchor population. Signed continuation endpoint means are mixed, with several uncertain intervals. First-touch bounce endpoint rates can sit near one half while payoff distributions differ. No optimization or trading edge is inferred from selected rates.

sections.description: Asia uses the inferred New York 20:00–03:00 window. Return is one-minute range contact with the lagged evolving VWAP ±1-tick zone; a gap or reference overtake alone is not contact.
notes: Intervals are marginal 95% shared-ISO-week cluster percentile bounds. Horizons have different eligible populations; use common-50 evidence for paired horizon curves.
Signed continuation is the next-open-to-terminal-close move in the departure direction; no fill, cost, stop or net profitability model is implied.

sections.description: Response entry is the next two-minute open after the touch candle closes. Endpoint bounce means terminal movement in the original excursion-side direction, not which barrier was hit first.

sections.body: Completed two-minute HLC3 is weighted by bar volume; population sigma is volume weighted. A first fresh strict close beyond two sigma is selected within a causal parent excursion. Entry is the next two-minute open. Primary touch is source one-minute range overlap with the tick-rounded ±one-tick evolving VWAP zone known at minute open; gap or reference overtake alone is not touch. Touch response begins after its containing two-minute candle closes. Upper departure continuation and upper-arrival bounce are long; lower counterparts are short. Continuation delta is departure-side sign multiplied by terminal close minus next-open entry, in native product points; fade is its negative, not a separately estimated difference. Bounce endpoint probability tests the signed terminal response, not a first-barrier winner or a trading win rate. Unavailable horizons are excluded from eligible outcome denominators. Saved marginal 95% intervals use shared ISO-week cluster draws.
sections.title: Definitions and methods

sections.body: Previously viewed, retrospectively complete history is exploratory: ES/NQ eligible dates begin in 2021 and GC in 2016, ending September 18, 2026. Anchors and thresholds are dependent. Bootstrap zero/all-success cells have unresolved boundary uncertainty, not certainty. Sparse support and exclusions remain in the saved coverage table. No order-flow delta, fills, costs, intraminute barrier order or realized profitability was tested. The optional Pine companion has not been independently compiled in its native environment.
